@internal Result of a set_cwd request. Every non-ok outcome leaves the working directory unchanged — but trust may already have been durably recorded when the request carried a valid attestation (a busy rejection or relocation failure after the latch does not unlatch it; the consent was for the directory, not the attempt). Internal failures (e.g. the transcript move failed and was rolled back) arrive as a control_response error instead.
@internal Runs at the hook author's explicit request (cloud: 'device' in its settings entry): it starts in the project folder, and its command may not be pinned to a script the session cannot change.
@internal Runs to paint over `text`, disjoint and ascending by `start`; the app paints them as given, with no range logic of its own. Omitted when there are none, never empty.

@internal Sent by the session client to a worker that advertises turn_handoff in its external_metadata: hand over a turn whose final assistant message holds tool calls that have not run. The worker answers at once — success {status: "accepted"} (validated and queued; the messages are appended at the start of the turn that runs the calls, the last one echoed back as an assistant event before any call runs; a request that runs nothing (see tool_use_ids) for the same turn as one still queued to run replaces it), success {status: "duplicate"} (every named call is already taken by an earlier delivery or answered; nothing runs — taken, not necessarily ran; or, for a turn that runs nothing, its calls are already answered by other lines, or the same turn is already pending in that shape or running), or an error whose message starts with its code and a colon: turn_handoff_disabled, invalid_handoff, unsupported_tool, unknown_tool, recovered_by_restart (this worker restarted after the turn was appended and its recovery set the turn's unrun calls aside; this request will not run or close them), expired (the request names calls to run and the session service has held it for over 30 minutes, by the created_at of the frame that delivered it: the service hands a request that no worker answered to every later worker of the session; nothing is appended or taken, and a request that runs nothing is never refused for its age). Accepted calls get the permission evaluation of the worker (rules, the permission mode, can_use_tool to the client); their tool_result messages and the model continuation follow on the event stream as in any turn.

@internal Sent with decision_reason_type 'rule', for an MCP tool's ask that has none, for the default prompt of Write or Edit with no reason type, and for that of Read, Write or Edit with 'workingDir' and the plain outside-the-working-directories decision_reason. true = when the frame was built, nothing asked for a person on this call but the default prompt for a tool that no rule allows and, at most, a tool policy that the host itself pushed (permission_policy 'always_ask'): no other ask rule that the permission check applies to the call, no hook's or plugin's ask, no PermissionRequest hook, no organization ceiling, no plan-mode floor, no safety check, no ask or veto on a standing grant of the tool's own, no auto-mode classifier active for the call. false = something else did, or may have. It says nothing of WHY the host pushed that policy, which only the host knows; nothing of whose server the tool is (see mcp_server), so a host answers only for a tool that it holds a person's grant for (a file tool apart, below); and nothing of what changes after the frame is sent. For a file tool it says nothing of where the path lies, so a host answers only for a path that it has judged itself. Absent on other reason types, on any other tool's ask without a reason type (Read's included), wherever a request is listed, mirrored or passed on again (pending_permission_requests), and from older versions.
@internal Server-asserted ingest path of the demoted delivery, copied at classification from the message-level `inbound_origin`.

@internal Set for some errors that Claude Code wrote for the model. `text` is a short line shown to people instead of `replaces`, the line the error would otherwise show. If the error no longer shows `replaces`, for example because a PostToolUse hook rewrote it, the error's own line is shown

@internal Set on a `message_stop` that Claude Code produced itself, after it stopped reading the response that `message_stop` closes because the API's stream failed, stalled or ended early, or because the turn was interrupted. That response's content blocks at index `from_block_index` and above have no assistant message and will never get one, so a consumer that drew or stored them from stream events, and holds no assistant message for them, can remove them, even a block that has had its `content_block_stop`. Nothing is stated about lower blocks: some may have no assistant message, and what follows may repeat or replace them. What follows can be, among others, a retry (a new `message_start`), the same request without streaming (assistant messages under another id, with no `message_start` before them), an assistant message that reports the error, or nothing. A plugin can add content blocks of its own to a response, and those do get assistant messages under the same id, emitted before this event. Absent on every other `message_stop` (the API's own, one produced for a response that had arrived whole, one where Claude Code cannot be sure), on Remote Control (interactive terminal) sessions and from older producers. An absent key states nothing: a block with no assistant message yet may still get one.

@internal Some files a user message sent by reference (file_attachments) did not arrive where Claude can read them, and Claude was told so in that message's text or in a later note; the turn runs on without them. A host can use it to tell the person who sent them; a session with Remote Control on also sends it to its Remote Control clients itself. Sent once the message is queued, or later when a download or a save that runs beside its turn fails, or both; only for a message that reached the session through Claude Code Remote or over Remote Control, never for input a local host writes; whenever Claude is told, and for the same files. Queued counts as told: a message that a Stop then clears from the queue, or that a UserPromptSubmit hook then blocks, still sends it, though Claude never reads that message. Nothing is sent when every file arrives, when the message is refused or has no uuid (over Remote Control, one not in UUID form counts as none), for another session's message that was first held for approval, when the only files lost are those over the count limit of a message in which an entry carries a sha256 digest, or for a picture that reached Claude inside the message and whose saved copy alone was lost; on claude-code-server the same holds for a text file whose copy was to be written late, at a use of the tool container. A file whose entry carries a sha256 (another session's transfer) is reported to Claude by name instead, and is listed here only under 'not_finished'. Each event states the whole list for its message: a save lost after the message was queued, or a delivery to a new worker, states it again, so keep the last one per message_uuid. If its files all arrive that time nothing is sent, and the earlier event stands. One exception: a worker that takes over a turn already begun, or is sent again a message that its transcript already holds, may fetch and save the message's files again, except pictures and files with a sha256. Its event lists only those it could not fetch or save, so it can leave out a picture an earlier event listed, and can list a file the earlier worker did save.

@internal Source code the surface draws with its own highlighter: `language` a highlight.js id or alias, else inferred from `path` (never read); `startLine` numbers a line gutter; under `format: "diff"` `source` is unified-diff hunks the engine checked parse; `wrap` is `wrap` (the default) or `truncate-end`, which cuts long lines with an ellipsis. `source` is bounded and free of control characters as the engine validated it; no children.
@internal Starting budget (tokens) for totalTokensReminder 'padded-countdown' mode. Defaults to 15000000. Server-controlled via GrowthBook; env var CLAUDE_CODE_TOTAL_TOKENS_REMINDER_BUDGET overrides.

@internal Style overrides the surface applies while the pointer is over the nearest keyed Box above the element, or over any member of the hover group `scope` names (a string of the drawing plugin's; two plugins never share a group): a Box's `borderStyle`, `borderColor`, `borderDimColor`, `backgroundColor`, `display` ("flex", revealing a Box drawn "none") and the offsets of a placed Box; a Text's or a Button label's colors and styles. Plain data the engine validated; nothing that moves a sibling.

@internal Subagents started through the Agent tool in this session, as running totals (forked skills, workflows, teammates and other internal agents are not counted; two sessions in one process keep separate counts). Cumulative like modelUsage: read the latest result rather than summing across results; a resumed session starts fresh and a mid-session /clear zeroes it, though a background subagent that outlives the /clear still records its outcome, so completed, failed and killed can then exceed spawned. A result that was held back while background subagents finished carries the counts as of when it is written to the stream, as do its total_cost_usd, duration_api_ms and modelUsage (and usage where that is a running total; a per-turn main-loop usage keeps its turn-end value). Omitted by hosts without a local Agent tool and on crash/startup-error results; all zeros until the Agent tool starts or refuses a subagent. A remote (isolation: remote) launch counts as spawned but never reports an outcome. Per-subagent detail is on the task_started / task_notification events.

@internal Submits a /feedback report (description + current session transcript + sanitized error log) to api.anthropic.com/api/claude_cli_feedback using the CLI's auth and redaction. Runs the same getFeedbackUnavailableReason() policy checks as the terminal /feedback command — when feedback is disabled (org policy, env kill-switch) or cannot be sent (3P provider, no Anthropic credentials) the response carries unavailable_reason instead of an error. When the server refuses the submission for the organization or the report's content, the response carries both unavailable_reason and failure_reason. A request carrying save_locally gets the terminal's local save instead: the report is written to a redacted zip on this machine and the response carries bundle_path, nothing sent — except where feedback is disabled, which still refuses.
@internal Success payload answering remote_tool_call: the result under one fixed key, never spread at the top level.
@internal Summary of Stop/SubagentStop hook execution at turn end — which hooks ran, their output, and whether any prevented continuation. From internal SystemMessage 'stop_hook_summary'.
@internal Summary of what happened while the user was away (background tasks completed, notifications accumulated). From internal SystemMessage 'away_summary'.

@internal The CLI itself stopped the running turn so a user's rapid follow-up message is answered at once, exactly as a priority 'now' message would have (running shell commands are backgrounded, not killed). Sent at the moment of the stop, so it precedes the stopped turn's result frame (terminal_reason aborted_streaming or aborted_tools) and its members' 'cancelled' command_lifecycle frames (it can also precede the follow-up's own 'queued' command_lifecycle frame): a host renders that turn as superseded by the follow-up rather than as interrupted, does not resend its messages, and treats only preempted_by_uuid as picked up. At most one per burst: the turn the follow-up starts is never preempted this way. Emitted on the stdout stream in -p/SDK sessions only, and only to a consumer that declared rapidFollowupPreempt on its initialize request, while the feature's rollout flag is on: without both, the turn is not stopped at all. Explicit 'now' and 'later' priorities never produce it.

@internal The CLI's active model at connect time. Remote Control clients (web/mobile) sync their model dropdown TO this value on connect instead of sending set_model with their own default — without it, connecting from a phone silently switches the terminal's model (CC-2659).

@internal The CPU time of the turn, by thread, in whole ms. Each key is a state of process_turn_states, or between_turns for the process_cpu_ms_between_turns stretch; each value holds the fields below. Sent by about one worker process in 4,096, drawn as the process starts or, in one started ahead of its session, when it takes up its session (CLAUDE_CODE_THREAD_CPU_ONE_IN in its environment at that moment changes the rate: 1 is every process, 0 none). one_in: the N of the one-in-N draw that picked this process. CCR, the session service, counts only reports with one_in 4096, so that a process started at another rate cannot weigh on the sums. startup_timing.process_stretch_threads holds the same fields for each of process_stretches' stretches, except to_spare_loaded and to_claim in a process started ahead of its session, which is drawn only after them; in the first stretch of any other process guest_steal_ms counts from just after the process started, and the check below of the main thread's time against the turn's does not apply. Threads are grouped by the name that the kernel shows, which is compared with a fixed list and never sent. main: the process's first thread, whatever its name, which runs the CLI's JavaScript. gc: JavaScriptCore's threads that help with garbage collection; the main thread's own part counts under main. jit: JavaScriptCore's compiler threads. warm_up: the thread that Bun names JSCWarmUp. allocator: the allocator's thread that looks for freed memory to give back to the kernel. http: Bun's thread for the sockets of fetch(). pool: Bun's threads for work handed off the main thread, such as file reads. other: every other name. <group>_cpu_ms is the user plus system time of the group's threads, which the kernel counts in nanoseconds. <group>_system_ms is the system part of it, which the kernel estimates from samples at its timer's ticks and gives for a thread only in steps of 10 ms: each time a state is entered it can be up to 10 ms high or low for each thread, so it can exceed <group>_cpu_ms, and it means something only summed over many reports. Either is left out where it rounds to 0. process_cpu_ms and process_system_ms are the same two for the whole process, counted as in process_cpu_ms_between_turns and not in steps. process_cpu_ms less the sum of the <group>_cpu_ms is the time of threads that ended: what each used after it was last read, or all of it if it was never read, give or take a few ms, because the kernel updates a running thread's count only at timer ticks. run_wait_ms: how long the process's threads, added up, were ready to run and waited for one of the virtual machine's CPUs. guest_steal_ms: how long the virtual machine's CPUs, added up, had work and waited for the host, whichever program the work was, in steps of 10 ms; left out where /proc/stat could not be read. Stolen time counts as CPU time of the thread that was running, unless the kernel was built with CONFIG_PARAVIRT_TIME_ACCOUNTING. A reading is made at each change of state and every 5 s, because JavaScriptCore ends a helper or compiler thread that has been idle for 10 s. Each costs the main thread a fraction of a millisecond, which counts in the time that follows it. Present where process_turn_states is, in such a process, unless a reading by thread failed on the turn, a value came out below 0, or a pause of the virtual machine may have been booked as CPU time: two readings came more than 15 s apart, which a main thread blocked for 10 s also causes, so the longest synchronous stretches are missing, or the main thread's time over the turn came out more than 20 ms longer than the turn. between_turns is left out where process_cpu_ms_between_turns is, and for the same failures over that stretch.

@internal The `anthropic-client-platform` value of the app a person sent the first of messages from. Left out when no person sent that message, as in a scheduled run. When it names one of the Remote Control apps (isRemoteControlAppPlatform) and that message is not one from another session, the worker marks the message as sent by a person, as it marks a user message that arrives with that value, so the turn counts as started by a person for the calls it runs and for those the model makes afterwards, and the turn the worker runs carries that value as its client platform, as a turn for such a user message does (per-turn telemetry, and tools that read which app the person is on). The member is never a reason to refuse the request: without it, or with any other value, the message is appended unmarked and the turn carries no platform.

@internal The `press_id` of the press whose own handler's call made this `$.prompt.fill`, awaited by that handler or not: the engine's word, which no plugin's argument and no `prompt.fill` hook can set, change or remove. Sent only to the client whose `client_id` the press carried. Absent in every other case: a fill from a hook, a timer no press's handler set, a field or a pick; a fill from code another plugin's call reached; a fill whose text or placement a `prompt.fill` hook changed; a press whose argument a hook changed before its handler ran; a press that carried no `press_id`, or one and no `client_id`; and an answered press, once a newer press of the same plugin that carried an id is answered too. It speaks for this one write, not for the draft the text lands in. The engine checks neither the age of the id nor how often it is named: that is the host's.

@internal The `press_id` of the press whose own handler's call made this `$.ui.copy`, awaited by that handler or not. Only the engine sets it: no plugin's argument and no `ui.copy` hook can set or change it, and a hook that changes the text or surface removes it. Set only on a request addressed to the client whose `client_id` the press carried. Absent from any other copy: one from a hook, a field, a pick, a timer no press's handler set, or code reached through a plugin's method, its own included; one whose press argument a hook changed before its handler ran; one whose press carried no `press_id` or no `client_id`; and one made once its press and a newer press of the same plugin that carried an id are both answered. The engine checks neither the age of the id nor how often it is named, on copies and fills alike: that is the host's.

@internal The asking client's id on the session's roster of attached surfaces: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`. Two phones are two ids on one surface; a client that never attaches is the engine's `<surface>:default`, which no wire id can spell.

@internal The asking worker's life, as the worker states it. A client ignores an ask below the newest worker epoch it has heard and never addresses its announce by this value: the announce goes to the epoch last heard, and the worker's stale_worker_epoch answer teaches the client the current one.
@internal The body: the plugin's words, cleaned of control characters and cut to 1000 characters. Plain text: draw it as a text node, never as markup.
@internal The calling plugin's registry name, as the hooks engine knows it (never plugin-settable).
@internal The calling plugin's registry name, as the hooks engine knows it (never plugin-settable). One status line per plugin.

@internal The calling plugin's registry name, as the hooks engine knows it (never plugin-settable). Written as the registry spells it and not cleaned as `title` is, so a host must scrub it. Show it after the host's own word that a mod sent it, so neither it nor the title can pass for the app's own.

@internal The chain's argument as it reached the element's own handler (`plugin`, `element`, `component`, `requestId`, `surface`, and `kind`/`value` for an input or pick, as hooks above left them): the surface runs the frame's closure with it. Absent when a hook withheld the press; the closure does not run.

@internal The container's project root, for path translation on the device: absolute, no '.' or '..' segments, no backslash, no control or format characters. Untrusted by the device all the same, which must containment-check every translated path.

@internal The conversation, or the git repository it runs in, shows a known kind of development work, for hosts that key tooling on it (Claude Code Desktop opens its iOS Simulator entry point on ios_app). Sent with trigger as its only other payload. Per conversation per process, each kind is sent at most once from conversation evidence and at most once from the project scan. Conversation evidence is sent when it first completes, or at startup when a resumed conversation already has it. Project evidence comes from a CLI process in print mode (-p), which is how the Agent SDK and Claude Code Desktop start it. It is sent at startup, after each conversation_reset, and at the first message of a conversation whose earlier scan did not find every kind. Either can arrive before system/init. A rewind or compaction never retracts it and only a conversation_reset starts over. Treat each kind as a sticky fact about the conversation: a client that needs only the kind can ignore repeats, and one that needs to know what set it off reads trigger.
@internal The device digested the hook's script at start-up and re-verifies those bytes before each run; the digest itself is not sent.
@internal The draft the Composer is to show: the request's own, or a hook's rewrite of it.
@internal The element holding the ring as the engine records it now: the reported one, a hook's redirect the surface should focus, or null on the container.

@internal The engine's requests this client answers on a plugin's behalf: `ui_copy` (its clipboard), `ui_prompt_read` / `ui_prompt_fill` / `ui_prompt_paint` / `ui_prompt_suggest` (its composer), `ui_read_selection` (what the person has selected in its page). The engine sends each only to a client that named it; a client that never names any (or names `[]`) is never asked, so `$.ui.copy` to its surface answers `no-clipboard`, the prompt calls the empty box / false and `$.ui.selection` nothing, as before. On a repeated ui_attach a given list (including `[]`) replaces the earlier one and an absent field keeps it: send `[]` to stop answering.
@internal The entry carries an if-condition, evaluated on the device; the condition text never leaves it.

@internal The fix a host can offer for a tool result, stamped from structured producer state (never parsed from the result text). Kinds: mcp_needs_auth, mcp_disabled, mcp_required_missing, auth_expired, auth_overridden, auth_missing_scope, design_needs_authorization, sandbox_violation, outside_reads_blocked, memory_paused, feature_disabled, policy_denied, spawn_arg_limit (the command's exec image exceeded the OS argument limit), staged_for_review (a settings-file write held for the machine owner's review). New kinds are additive; treat an unknown kind as absent.
@internal The hook's own timeout in seconds, when configured; the worker derives its deadline from it.

@internal The host of a multi-tenant worker shut the worker down while this turn ran. The shutdown was the first thing to abort the turn, and the turn is left for the session's next worker. The other frames of the ending, and terminal_reason, are the same as for a Stop from a client. Read this member to tell the two apart. A success result can have it, when the shutdown falls in a Stop hook. A result without it can also be the result of a shutdown. A shutdown that makes the turn write no interrupt marker does not set it, and older producers never set it.

@internal The host quit or updated while it served this request and wants the same connection back: the helper takes it up again or does not start, and never links. Absent or false is a start that links.

@internal The host's own id for this one press: 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'. A `$.prompt.fill` or `$.ui.copy` that the pressed element's own handler makes names it back as `answers_press` on the ui_prompt_fill or ui_copy. A value of any other shape is dropped as if absent and the press runs the same. Send `client_id` with it: the id is named back to that client alone, and the id of a press that carries no `client_id` is named back to no client. No hook and no handler is shown it. A CLI that predates the field ignores it.

@internal The host's own label for what started this turn (e.g. the desktop app's `scheduled-task`, `sleep-auto-resume`); `user`, an empty string or absent means a person sent it. For usage attribution; any other label also keeps a message with no origin, sent while a turn is running, from going out as the user's words, and keeps a message on claude-code-server from being marked as typed or clicked by a person.

@internal The host's view of which Claude in Chrome browser this session should use when several are connected to the account: `preferredDeviceId` is the browser its user picked last on that computer, `localDeviceIds` the relay device ids it knows to be running on that computer right now, `hostPlatform` that computer's OS (for the weaker same-OS label). Session memory only, never persisted; the built-in claude-in-chrome server reads them as its persisted pick and its on-this-computer set, so it defaults to that browser instead of asking. Hints only: nothing is selected unless it is in the live relay roster, and an empty list clears them.

@internal The id of the claude.ai connector this server proxies, for a host that keys the server by another name. The server must declare the same id in its own capabilities for the CLI to treat it as that connector. With or without that declaration, deny and ask rules, hook matchers and disallowed-tool lists that spell mcp__<connectorId> also reach this server's tools, and nothing that allows does; the id is read as a tool's name would spell it (a character other than a letter, a digit, '-' and '_' as '_'), and one that is then longer than 128 characters or holds '__' is not used for that. Read from initialize and mcp_set_servers, not --mcp-config, when the server is first registered.
@internal The instance's next props when a hook answered `{ props }`: the surface hands them to the frame, local state kept; absent leaves them.

@internal The keyboard moved in a site a remote surface draws: the engine records the hold and raises `ui.focus` for the element (origin `person`, or the element's plugin under `auto`); a hook may redirect it, which the answer then carries for the surface to follow.

@internal The largest delay, in whole ms, between the remote transport's stream-event flush timer falling due and its buffer being emptied, from the turn's first frame of visible reply text until this result was built. This is a lower bound on how late that timer fired. It is read on the wall clock, so a clock set forward adds to it. Capped at 60000. Absent when text_post_count is absent, or when the buffer was never emptied at or after a due time.
@internal The layer's runs over `text`, disjoint and ascending by `start`, replacing the ones it had; the app paints them as given. Omitted when there are none, never empty.
@internal The line the plugin gave: be ready for up to 10000 characters of it and then an ellipsis. Plain text: draw it as a text node, never as markup.

@internal The offset the engine holds for the window now, which the surface should show: when allowed, the reported offset clamped to the layout (`by` rows over the engine's own window for a move down from a followed end or a move from the row of a report it had not landed, or a hook's rewrite); the offset the engine held before the move when denied; a plugin's offset when its move landed meanwhile; the reported offset as sent for `no such site`.

@internal The originating system local_command row's wire-form content (escaped frames), carried on the loop-synthesized local-command twin. Round-tripped so toInternalMessages rebuilds the internal system row on a bridge/SDK history replay — replay then matches the live session, where that row is model-visible — instead of dropping the output or replaying the twin's decoded display text. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content`.
@internal The pane the surface shows: the last opened or focused, never displacing one the person holds; null with none open.
@internal The pane's tab label: the `title` its latest open gave, else its id. Plugin-authored text the engine bounded and freed of control characters: draw it as a text node, never as markup.

@internal The person scrolled a site a remote surface draws (a pane's body, the band): the engine records the layout reported and raises `ui.scroll` with origin `person` for a move of `by` rows onto `offset` (clamped to the layout; while the site follows its end, a move down is `by` rows from that end instead; and `by` rows over the engine's own window when `offset` is the last report's offset moved by `by` and the engine did not land that last report where it said); a hook may rewrite or deny it, and the answer carries the offset the surface should show. Send it throttled to the surface's frame; reports arriving while one is in flight for the instance are folded (`by` summed) into one that follows and answered alike, in order.

@internal The person's close of a pane on a remote surface: runs the `ui.close` chain with origin `person` (a hook may keep the pane open) and answers whether it closed. The surface removes the pane only on `closed: true`; the ui_panes push that follows drops it too.
@internal The plugin whose hook drew the Input, as its `press.plugin` carried it.
@internal The plugin whose hook drew the Select, as its `press.plugin` carried it.
@internal The plugin whose hook drew the pressed element, as the tree carried it.
@internal The plugin's full id, `name@marketplace`, as the hooks engine loaded it (never plugin-settable). Two plugins sharing a name differ here. A side-loaded plugin reads `name@inline`.
@internal The plugin's full id, as on ui_notify (never plugin-settable). Only notifications of this source are touched.
@internal The plugin's pinned line, replacing its previous one; null removes it. Be ready for up to 10000 characters of it and then an ellipsis. Plain text: draw it as a text node, never as markup.
@internal The plugin's registry name, as the hooks engine knows it (never plugin-settable).

@internal The plugins something of `tree` or `props` may be owed to, by the name each is loaded under, in chain order: those whose `ui.render` hook ran for this ask and did more than hand on (told one by one for the vscode surface; elsewhere neighbours that share the sandbox are told together), or every plugin hooked on the instance where that is not known. Plugins the binary carries are left out, so an empty list says the drawing is Claude Code's own. The engine's word, which no hook can set: what a surface marks a drawing with. Absent from a CLI that predates the field: whose the drawing is, is then not known.
@internal The report a 'send' or 'flagged' hand-back delivered, for a client to render instead of content

@internal The report a 'send' or 'flagged' hand-back delivered, the same shape as `handbackReport` on AgentToolCompletedOutput: when present, render it instead of `summary`, with its `warning`, if it has one, above its `text`. Absent for 'withheld'; if it is absent for another value too, show `summary`.

@internal The request's `path`, exactly as sent, on every success reply whose `absPath` is what that path resolved to. If it differs from the path you sent, the reply answers another request under the same request_id: drop it and keep waiting. Compare the reply's `anchor` with your anchor's kind as well. Both can still match for another file where what the path is resolved against changes between requests (the live cwd, an as_written look-up) or isn't in the reply (which repository, for the anchor kind repo). Absent where `absPath` is itself the path as sent (Remote Control, and a session that reads through a tool container), from the engine's readFile, and in replies of an older CLI. It does not prove who wrote the reply.

@internal The request_id of a rewind_conversation control request that the client sent ahead of this one, when the turn is meant only for the conversation as that rewind leaves it. A worker that advertises requires_rewind_request_id: true in turn_handoff_available reads it; a worker without that key ignores it and appends the turn whether or not the rewind was made, and the request may start a new worker whose build the client cannot know, so a client sends the member only once every worker that could read it has the key. A worker that reads it appends the turn only if that rewind is the last one it carried out (answered rewound: true), the last user or assistant message is still the one that rewind left at the end, and nothing it holds waits to be appended ahead of the turn (a turn in progress, or a message it received since). Otherwise it appends nothing and runs no call, and answers an error that starts "invalid_handoff: required_rewind_" and then one word: unknown, this worker has carried out no rewind (it replaced the worker that answered that request, or the request was refused or not read yet); other, its last rewind is a different request (the named one was refused here, not read yet, or followed by another); moved_on, it made that cut and the conversation has changed since; lines_waiting, it made that cut and something waits to be appended first. After unknown or other, go by the rewind's own answer where one was given, bearing in mind that a rewound: false of persist_failed or state_changed can still leave the cut for the next worker, and that the same rewind delivered again after its cut was stored answers target_not_found, except on a later worker that loaded the stored record of that cut, where the record names the row it cut at: that worker answers it rewound: true again, with the same fields, and then takes the turn. A client that saw rewound: true and is then answered unknown may send the turn again without the member: the cut stands, though the new worker may have appended lines since, so the turn lands at the conversation's end, not necessarily right after the cut. After other, moved_on or lines_waiting do not send the turn again without the member: the conversation is not, or may no longer be, as that rewind left it. The check is skipped once any of the turn's messages is in the conversation or queued from an earlier delivery: a request sent again after that is answered as without the member. A value that is not a string is refused (invalid_handoff).

@internal The resolved feedback mode (getFeedbackMode) for host UIs that offer a feedback dialog, so they can say up front that a report is refused or saved on this machine, instead of learning either only after the user has written and sent it.

@internal The server_received_wall_ms of the user message that user_message_uuid names, copied unchanged, so the session server can measure from its own receipt to request_sent_wall_ms (two machines' clocks) without keeping the receipt time. Present only with request_sent_wall_ms, and only when that message carried a positive finite number there; absent from older producers.

@internal The session indicator (the CLAUDE_CODE_FOOTER_INDICATOR environment variable, else the footer_indicator_<text> capability of the main model, else bootstrap client_data.footer_indicator) that the terminal renders as a "◆ <text>" pill in the prompt footer — an opaque status note operators set per cohort (e.g. to prove a test config reached the session). Carried on `system/init` and the `initialize` response so a host UI (Claude Desktop, IDE webviews) can render the same pill. Absent when nothing is configured; hosts should then render nothing. The client_data source is read from the CLI's cached bootstrap data, so a label configured there after that cache was last written first appears on a later `system/init`.

@internal The session's instruction files add up to more than the recommended limit. Numbers only: the host words the warning in the person's language. Sent to Claude Desktop's Code tab alone, at most once per process, on a conversation's first turn after system/init; never stored in the transcript. Safe to ignore: a host that does not recognize this subtype shows nothing.

@internal The session's name, for a host that shows it, such as an IDE editor tab. A headless (print mode) session sends it at startup when the session already has a name, and again after each change to the name (not an AI-generated title), including a rename the host itself sent with `rename_session`. A name that another process writes to the transcript arrives when this process next reads the end of its transcript: after about 32 KB of its own transcript writes, or at a compaction. A cleared name is not sent. The same name can arrive more than once, for example when it is set again, so a host should treat a repeated name as no change. The frame can arrive before the system/init message that first names its session_id, for example at startup or after /clear. A host that learns the session id from system/init can hold the name until then.

@internal The snapshot of the user's claude.ai memory that the client showed its model with the turn's user message. Used on a request that names calls to run, or on a history request (no calls named, not stopped) if the session holds none of its messages yet: the worker writes it ahead of the first of messages, with uuid as the line's uuid, as a cowork_memory_context attachment line like those it writes for snapshots it fetches itself, and then adds no copy of that version. version and content are both strings for a snapshot, both null to withdraw an earlier one. The member is never a reason to refuse the request: one that is malformed, that has a version without content or the reverse, or whose uuid is also that of one of messages, of relay_marker or of a line the session's transcript holds, is ignored, and the turn goes on without the line.

@internal The system line that starts the prompt-cache relay for this conversation: uuid is the line's uuid, and content is the marker, a JSON string whose anchor_line_uuid is the uuid of the first of messages; other fields of the line are ignored. Only a worker that advertises relay_marker: true in turn_handoff_available uses it, on a request that names calls to run, or on a history request (no calls named, not stopped) if the session holds none of its messages yet. It is never a reason to refuse the turn: when the member is not such a line, or the worker does not use the marker, the request is answered as without it.
@internal The template script bytes, base64; decoded size must not exceed the template's cap (at most 256 KiB).

@internal The thinking.display that Claude Code put in the API request body for the response that streamed this frame's thinking block. It has the same source and meaning as `thinking_display` on a stream event. Sent only on a frame whose one content block is a thinking block that was streamed, and only when the body had a display. Older CLI versions never send it, and a CLI that rebuilt its history from SDK frames does not send it when it replays that history. An absent key states nothing. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content` — so it is not replayed to the model.

@internal The time that passed in the process_cpu_ms_between_turns stretch, by a clock that never runs backward. Time while the process is stopped counts; time while its virtual machine is paused may not.
@internal The time to raise it, epoch ms, for a moment fixed on the clock at most 7 days ahead: the client books it as `delay_ms` books. Never sent beside `delay_ms`.

@internal The tool_use blocks of the last message to run, each of a tool named in the turn_handoff entry of the worker external_metadata; all run in one batch, then the model continues once. May be empty, and then nothing runs and no model turn follows: with every call the turn carries answered within it (the last message holding none), the worker appends the turn as history and, once the lines are stored, echoes the last assistant message that holds a call; with stopped, the user stopped the turn before its calls ran. In both cases, when a leading part of the turn is already in the conversation from an earlier delivery, only the rest is appended; where its first assistant message repeats the id of the last one already there, as messages allows, the two are sent to the model as one message.

@internal The turn so far, in conversation order: the user's message, any [assistant, tool_result] rounds already answered elsewhere, and last an assistant message (thinking blocks with their signatures, text, and the tool_use blocks to run). Every message carries a uuid, kept as the transcript line's; none of the messages, and none of the tool_use ids they hold, may already be in the conversation — the turn is appended once, whole, never merged with lines already there (except as tool_use_ids describes for a turn that runs nothing). No two assistant messages share a message id, among these or with the conversation, with one exception, for a worker whose turn_handoff entry has shared_message_id: an assistant message that holds tool_use blocks only may repeat the id of the assistant message before it where every message between them, at least one, holds only tool_result blocks for that earlier message's calls. The two are then sent to the model as one message, its calls followed by their results, so a client does this only for calls of one Messages API response that it ran one after another. A request that names calls to run is refused (invalid_handoff) unless its first message is a user message, not empty and not a tool_result.
@internal The user-settings defaultMode the one-shot auto-default nudge should offer to replace with auto. IDE hosts only; absent when the user isn't eligible.

@internal The wire version the worker will speak with this machine, or null when the worker will forward nothing to it: no wire version in common, or interface version ranges that do not fit. The machine stays listed.

@internal The worker life (system/init's worker_epoch) that this interrupt is for, as a JSON number. Written only on an interrupt that a service sends by itself and that must not outlive the worker it was meant for. Never written on a person's Stop, not even as a null or a 0 for 'unset': a Stop must hold across a restart. Read by a claude-code-server tenant alone, before every other member and whatever they say. A worker of another life takes none of an interrupt's steps (it still counts as a person's presence, as every interrupt does), marks the request processed, so that no later worker is served it, and answers with a stale_worker_epoch error; take the new number from the next system/init, not from the error's text. Any other value that is present (a null, a 0, a fraction, a string such as '7') is refused the same way with an invalid_worker_epoch error, never read as absent. Both errors carry the token as error_code and list no still_queued: they are no receipt. The worker of the stated life, every other host that handles an interrupt, and an older tenant handle the request as if the member were absent, and no capability says which a worker is; a client that relays its host's Stop to a hosted session drops the member.

@internal True on an initialize reply that goes over the pipes of the host that spawned this CLI, from a CLI that ranks another PreToolUse hook's ask above the host's own: where a hook that this host registered asks, and any other hook asks on the same call, the can_use_tool request carries the other hook's reason, whichever finished first. A plugin's hooks module may still re-word an ask, and a hook may copy the host's words (docs/desktop-host-contract.md D65a). Absent for a remote client, whose hooks are never the host's own, in a Cowork cloud session or a Code cloud worker, and on CLIs that predate it, which may send the host's own reason even when another hook asked: there a host must not take its own reason to mean that nobody else asked.

@internal True only where permissions.blockFileToolReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories is in force: the read and write blocks then count only the starting directory, --add-dir, and permissions.additionalDirectories (fully qualified, or ~ or ~/…; a relative entry does not count) in --settings or in a push, and none that a policy tier adds. Never true in a background session, whose launch is replayed from files that the account can write, nor while the starting directory has moved outside both the one that headless start-up began with (after any --worktree) and the added folders named above. False or absent: do not rely on this. docs/desktop-host-contract.md D112 lists what can still move those blocks.

@internal True when no pane has that id after the call: it closed, or none had it (no chain ran). False when a `ui.close` hook kept it open, or a close of it was already being decided (the ui_panes push says how that one ended).

@internal True when the CLI has analytics/telemetry disabled (privacy level, DO_NOT_TRACK, or 3P provider). IDE clients use this to hide per-message thumbs feedback UI since the rating event would be a no-op.

@internal True when the org's allow_product_feedback policy is false (ZDR/HIPAA). IDE clients use this to hide feedback surfaces (thumbs, session survey) whose events the CLI would drop at the proxy boundary anyway.

@internal True when the request is a client's Send now on a message that is waiting, not its Stop: it asks that the waiting messages reach the model now, as the terminal's send-now key does. It is not a Stop: it makes no later turn start aborted, cancels nothing that is queued, and ends no background task, subscription or other thing outside the running turn that a Stop ends. What it does depends on what the CLI holds when it reads the request, and the response's send_now says which. Without message_uuid every waiting user message counts, which may be another than the one pressed. With no user message waiting at the CLI it does nothing: a message the running turn has already taken in, or was started for, is being answered. With one waiting that is not in the queue yet (received and still being admitted, or already taken for the next turn), that the running turn is taking in at that moment, or with no turn under way, it also does nothing: the message runs when its place comes. With a person's message in the queue behind a turn under way, the CLI chooses how that turn makes way: it moves what the turn waits on to the background so that the turn takes the message in (and, if that fails, stops the turn later as a priority 'now' message does, without a marker); over a turn that is compacting the conversation by itself, it first lets the compaction end, so that the summary is kept, and then moves what the turn waits on, or stops the turn at its next model request as a priority 'now' message does, without a marker; or it aborts that turn at once as a plain interrupt does (running tools are ended, the interruption marker is written, the result is an error_during_execution); what was queued ahead of the message still runs before it. Either way a sender learns that the turn has ended from the turn's result, not from this response. The message must already be at the CLI, or the request finds nothing waiting: a sender that still holds it delivers it first, or sends it with priority 'now', or sends a plain interrupt instead. Only the boolean true counts, and with cancel_queued:true the request is a Stop. Advertised by interrupt_send_now_v1 on system/init; a CLI without it handles the request as a plain interrupt.

@internal True when the server is reached through the cloud session's own MCP proxy, or is a claude.ai connector the session mounted: its sign-in is held there, never in this process, so a client offers no OAuth sign-in for it. Absent when false and on CLIs that predate the field.

@internal True when this Output carries only an async eval's late output: stdout is the lines the script logged after its settle, delivered as one batch to the PostToolUse hooks before it reaches the model. Never set on a settle or a result

@internal True: this Stop ends the turn and leaves running background agents and workflows alone, as a Stop does for a client that declared perTaskStopAffordance. A running observer still stops. Written by a client that has its own stop for each task, for a person's Stop that should end only the turn. Holds for this request alone, whatever a client declared at initialize. A CLI that does not read it treats the request as it treats any other, and a claude-code-server tenant ends those tasks whatever this says.

@internal Typed kind of the API error when is_api_error_message is true, for consumers that key on the cause instead of the message text (the text stays the fallback and may change). Absent when the error has no typed kind; new values are added over time, so treat an unknown value as absent. dlp_request_denied: the request was refused by the organization's data-loss-prevention policy — terminal for that request body; a consumer replaying history must not re-send it. claude_code_version_too_old: the API refused the request because this Claude Code build is below a required minimum version — the selected model's minimum, or an organization-policy floor; only the message text says which and names the versions, and the remedy is updating Claude Code. safety_monitor_blocked: a server-side safety monitor blocked the model's response for this turn; terminal for the turn, so a consumer replaying history must not re-send the prompt that led to it. effort_requires_thinking: the model refuses the requested effort level while thinking is off; api_error_params.effort names the level. advisor_incompatible: the configured advisor model cannot be paired with this request's model. tool_history_mismatch: the API rejected the conversation's tool_use/tool_result pairing (a tool_use without its result, an orphaned tool_result, a duplicate tool_use id); re-sending the same history fails the same way, and rewinding the conversation is the remedy. autocompact_thrashing: the context refilled to the limit right after each automatic compaction, repeatedly, so the turn stopped; something in context is too large for the window. pdf_too_large: a PDF is over the API's page or size limit. pdf_password_protected: a PDF is encrypted. stored_login_refused: the stored claude.ai login was about to go out while the API key helper set by the machine's administrator or the organization's settings isn't in effect, or its settings couldn't be confirmed; no request was sent, and the message text says who can clear it. media_removed: the API refused an image or a document in the conversation, so Claude Code leaves it out of the requests that follow. The frame comes either before the answer of a retry that already left it out, or as the error that ended the turn (the result then repeats this value). api_error_params.media_reason says why, and api_error_params.media which kind of block. Other kinds (pdf_too_large, pdf_password_protected) and some untyped errors also leave the block out, so the absence of this value does not mean that nothing was left out. no_response: no response arrived before the first-byte deadline on any attempt, usually a proxy or gateway that holds responses until they complete. tls_untrusted_ca: the API's TLS certificate comes from an authority this process does not trust, usually a TLS-inspecting proxy or a gateway signed by a private CA. gateway_content_type: a proxy between Claude Code and Amazon Bedrock rewrote Bedrock's event-stream response. connection_failed: Claude Code could not reach the API host (DNS, a refused connection, no route, a proxy that refused the tunnel) or lost the connection (an open connection was cut, or the response body ended early). An error with a TLS error code never carries it: the untrusted-authority codes are tls_untrusted_ca, and the other certificate and handshake codes (for example an expired, revoked or wrong-host certificate) have no typed kind. A connection that is cut during the TLS handshake arrives with a socket code such as ECONNRESET and carries it. The client's own request timeout and a connection error whose cause Claude Code cannot tell have no typed kind either. stream_idle_timeout: Claude Code's own idle timer gave up waiting for more of the response on an open stream. It says that the timer fired, not that the server stalled: a long gap in a slow answer, a proxy that holds the response back, or a sleep that the timer cannot tell from a stall (a short one, for example) fires it too. computer_slept: a Claude Code timer found that the machine slept through its wait for the response. A claude-code-server session never sends it, because its process is not the person's computer; there the same failure has no typed kind. provider_credentials: a third-party cloud provider (api_error_params.provider) refused the request's credentials or access; api_error_params.remedy says what fixes it. gateway_signin_required: the Cloud gateway provider is configured and nobody is signed in to it; no request was sent. gateway_session_expired: the Cloud gateway session expired; no request was sent; api_error_params.remedy is gateway_token when the token came from the environment, which signing in does not replace. api_key_auth_disabled: the organization turned off API key authentication and the active credential is an API key. org_disabled_credential: the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable belongs to a disabled organization and overrides the account sign-in. invalid_credential_header: a credential or header value (from the environment, a helper, or the saved sign-in) cannot be sent as an HTTP header; caught before the request was sent. model_requires_usage_credits: the model runs on usage credits for this account, and credits are off or the included allowance is used up. long_context_credits_required: a request over the 200K-token context boundary needs usage credits. consent_unanswered: the model now uses usage credits and the prompt to confirm went unanswered; nothing was sent. no_allowed_fallback: switching off the model was needed (the usage-credits prompt was declined) and the model policy allows no other model. model_substitution_disabled: switching off the model was needed and CLAUDE_CODE_NO_MODEL_FALLBACK forbids it. field_not_granted: the organization is not allowed to send a field in the request, and the message text says what to do. usage_limit_reached: the request was refused by the account's own usage limit, a plan limit (session, weekly or per-model) or a spend cap on usage credits; api_error_params.rate_limit_info says which and when it resets. The other refusals that share error rate_limit never carry it: an organization policy that turned the service off (no limit was reached, and no reset clears it), a temporary server throttle, a capacity switch-off, an entitlement refusal shown in the server's own words, or a 429 on an API key or a third-party cloud provider. empty_completion: the model ended its turn with no visible text, its one retry had no content block, and a repeat of that retry had no visible text, on a person's own prompt with no reply and no tool result after it; the turn ends as an error so that a host shows a failure and not a blank reply. malformed_tool_use_exhausted: the model's reply stopped for a tool call and held none, and the loop's retries ran out; terminal for the turn, so a consumer replaying history must not re-send the prompt by itself. unattended_start_limit: a cloud session's process that starts where an earlier one died carries on what that one left unfinished; by the session's record, as many processes as are allowed (a number that is configured; with none there is no limit) had already done so within 24 hours with no message from a person in between, and this one did not; no request was sent; terminal for the turn, so a consumer replaying history must not re-send the prompt that led to it; anything new sent to the session runs as usual; a person's message allows it again, and so does time, as earlier starts pass out of the 24 hours. unattended_start_unconfirmed: a cloud session's process did not carry on what an earlier one left unfinished, because it could not check whether it was allowed to: the session's record of such starts could not be read or written, or the check failed; no request was sent; not terminal: a later process may carry the turn on. network_edge_blocked: the firewall in front of Anthropic's API refused the request for its network location (an unsupported region, or a VPN, proxy or network routing through one) before it reached the API; no sign-in or credential changes this.

@internal Usage-limit grace signal. Follows the latest served main-loop or subagent response: set when it reports grace-zone utilization > 0 (the server reports that only to a request that sent `anthropic-usage-limit: extended`, tengu_lantern_spool), cleared when a response the limiter ran on reports none or, if the latest in-zone response named the grace window's reset, once that reset passes on this machine's clock. Side calls, and responses with no `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status` (the limiter did not run), are not read. A refused request's 429 is not read either, so while requests are refused the last value persists: still expire any UI derived from this field via resetsAt. While set, overageStatus allowed / allowed_warning means paid extra usage covers the overflow (nothing will be cut off). Stays true at hard exhaustion (status rejected); combine with status instead of reading this field alone as "still usable".

@internal What a Remote Control environment reports about this machine when it registers: 'off' reports nothing, 'basic' the OS, architecture and detected developer tools, 'full' also the names of MCP servers configured on this machine (never a repository's .mcp.json). When unset, the level comes from the feature rollout, which may be any of the three. Managed, --settings and user settings choose the level (the most restrictive wins); project and local settings can only lower it, never raise it. Read when Remote Control starts; lowering it later applies from the next registration, raising it from the next start.

@internal What a ui_render request with the press's `render` would have answered as the handler settled, through the same `ui.render` chain and with fresh handles. Absent when the press carried no `render` or one that does not read, when it was not handled, when the client it names is no longer attached, when a redraw of that instance was pushed during each of three draws, and when the draw was refused or failed: the page asks ui_render as before. The pushes do not change: a write the engine holds back to pace redraws, or made after this answer, is told by its ui_invalidate, and the page asks again.
@internal What heads the notification: the plugin's words, cleaned of control characters and cut to 120 characters, or the plugin's name. Plain text, and never the only sign of who sent it.

@internal What of this instance the asking surface's viewport shows now, for a transcript message (UserMessage, AssistantMessage, ToolUse, ToolResult, ToolGroup, CommandOutput, TurnDuration, InfoNotice): the extent, or null while the surface draws it outside its viewport. The engine hands it to the hooks as `e.props.onScreen` for this surface's ask alone (a rewrite of it is refused) and never carries one surface's report to another; leave it out when the surface does not track visibility, and ask again, coalesced to the surface's frame, when it changes, so the hooks re-run for the messages crossing the viewport's edges.
@internal What taking the row writes over the token, the caret after it; never empty.

@internal What the client-side input normalization read from process state (the working directory a leading `cd` was stripped against, the stamp applied to a Slack send) for the inputs in `wire_tool_inputs`, keyed by the same tool_use ids. Round-tripped with `wire_tool_inputs` so a replayed history can verify each recorded input against the normalized one exactly. Wrapper-level sibling — never inside `message.content`.

@internal What the input_attachments phase of time_to_request_phases_ms did on the turn, to tell a wait inside one attachment producer from a process that was busy. The producers are the calls of maybe() in getAttachments; their labels are a closed list. A pass starts them in two groups, first those that read the prompt's own text and then all the others, each group one producer after another without a break, and then waits for the group. slowest_producer is the label of the one whose result came longest after the last of its group had been started (or after its own start, where that was later), among those that began within the phase, and slowest_producer_ms is that time: it is the producer a pass waited on longest, and where every producer finished almost at once it says little; a background agent's pass that begins within the phase is timed with the turn's own (a new process's first turn has none), and its re-reads are not counted. Where slowest_producer_ms is well above cpu_ms that producer most likely waited (on a file, the network or a child process); a time_to_request_loop_lag_ms near slowest_producer_ms says instead that the thread itself stood still about that long (a blocking call, or a paused process). Where it is not well above cpu_ms the label tells little. cpu_ms and major_faults are time_to_request_cpu_ms's and time_to_request_major_faults's counters over this phase alone and are read the same way: cpu_ms far below the phase's time means the process was not computing; at or above it means computing, without saying whose. Where cpu_ms is absent, the phase's own time is what there is to compare slowest_producer_ms with. changed_files_reread is how many files the changed_files producer set out to read again in full because their modification time was later than the one recorded when the conversation last wrote or edited them (0 when it read none again, whether or not any file was a candidate; absent when the conversation's record of files was empty or the producer did not run). Present on turns where the input_attachments phase started, unless nothing of it is known. cpu_ms and major_faults are absent wherever time_to_request_cpu_ms is absent, and when the turn's first model request went out before the phase ended. touch_compare counts how the changed_files producer's compares ended in the main thread's pass (a subagent's are not counted). A compare checks a touched file against what the conversation last saw (its size, then its bytes), before deciding whether to read it again. same: the text had not changed, so it was not read again. differs: it had, so it was read again. partial_view and already_compared: the file was not compared (the conversation has seen only part of it or an older copy, or it was compared once already since the conversation last read or wrote it) and was read again. The rest are why a compare declined and the file was read again: link_on_path (the file could not be shown to be the one its path names: the file swapped or removed meanwhile, or on Linux a symbolic link on the way), leaf_link (the open met a symbolic link: at the file, or on macOS anywhere on the way), nlink (the file has a second hard link), not_regular, oversize, enoent (the file was gone) and other (anything else, errors included). Whole numbers; a zero count is left out, and touch_compare is absent when nothing was counted. The remaining members add up what the main thread's attachment passes (each time Claude Code gathers a turn's attachments) measured of themselves. Only a pass that began and ended within one run of the phase, before the turn's first model request went out, adds to them: not a subagent's or a background agent's (though slowest_producer can come from one), and not a pass with attachments switched off. setup_ms, prompt_producers_ms, ambient_start_ms, ambient_wait_ms and render_ms split each pass in order, each rounded down, so their sum is at most the phase's time: setup_ms, the work before any producer starts (such as working out which tools the tool announcements list and, on a conversation's first pass in the process, reading that list's earlier state from the transcript); prompt_producers_ms, starting the producers that read the prompt's own text (at-mentioned files, MCP resources, mentions of agents, skills and peers) and waiting for them; ambient_start_ms, starting every other producer, each one's work up to its first wait included, with no wait between starts, so the thread ran code throughout (computing, or a blocking call); ambient_wait_ms, waiting for those; render_ms, the rest: merging the producers' results, logging the attachments with their token estimates, and making each attachment into a message, the caller's time between messages included. producers is how many producers the passes started. token_counts is how many times the passes asked the API to count a file's tokens (an at-mentioned file, a text file that came with the message, or a changed file), which happens only for text estimated above a quarter of the Read tool's token limit. Both are present, 0 included, whenever a pass was kept. token_count_ms is the time at least one such count was under way, so counts that overlap are not added twice; it is absent when token_counts is 0, and on claude-code-server no request is made, so it stays near 0. changed_files_read_ms is the time at least one of the changed_files producer's Read calls was under way, their token counts included (absent when it made none). differs_files sorts the files counted under touch_compare's differs by their size on disk when compared, counting only the passes kept here, so the bands can add up to less than differs: size_under_25_kb, size_25_to_50_kb, size_50_to_256_kb and size_over_256_kb (1 KB is 1,024 bytes; a size on a boundary is in the band above it, except exactly 256 KB, which is in size_50_to_256_kb; size_over_256_kb only where the Read size limit has been raised). hash_only counts those of them for which the conversation kept only a hash of the earlier text, so that the model, if told, gets the file's name without a diff. In differs_files a zero count is left out, and it is absent when no compare in a kept pass ended in differs.

@internal What the surface paints under this pane's body while it is the one shown: a theme key, a raw color, or `transparent` for nothing; checked at open, yet parse it, never write it into a style. Absent, the surface's own look stands.

@internal What the turn was given to settle before its own prompt (the resume_ phases and turn_start_tool_run in time_to_request_phases_ms say how long that took): orphaned_permission (a permission answer whose pending request was lost, as when a worker restarts, so the tool call is settled with that answer), turn_handoff (a turn in progress that the session's client handed over), deferred_tool_use (a call a PreToolUse hook deferred), or none (resume_other is still reported, at about 0). A turn given more than one reports the first in that order. Present where time_to_request_phases_ms is.
@internal What to draw the first engine node with: the chain's rewrite of the props, or the input's own. Props under any later engine node do not cross (the ledger holding them is process-local).

@internal What to draw, or `Theme`, the session's theme, by `instance_id`. Under `theme` no hook draws: the engine answers itself, `props` of `plugin` with whichever of `colors`, `overrideColorScheme` and a still `backdrop` stands to `desktop` and `mobile`, and `{}` with none standing, with a scene and no `colors`, under another id or to any other surface. Under `backdrop` a mod's `ui.render` hook for `Backdrop` draws the scene that stands, with `props` of `scene`, `plugin`, `glass` and `overrideColorScheme` where a plugin said it.

@internal What was said aloud on a voice call alongside the session, handed over by the host as background. Honored from the host on local stdin, only on a message with isSynthetic true, shouldQuery false, text_not_typed true, a priority other than now, text-only content and no files or pastes; in any other shape the message is taken as a plain task notification. It starts no turn. The model reads the text inside a frame which says that nothing in it is a request or an approval. A note stored as its own row, and its replay, hold one fixed header line and then the host's text; a note folded into a running turn, and its replay, hold the host's text alone. With replayUserMessages on, the host gets the message back as a replay with this origin; a build that does not know the origin never sends the origin back. The optional members are taken from a local host only, and are stored and replayed with the origin; no request to a model or a classifier holds them. Send a note only to a process that says 'voice_call_talk_line_v1' in capabilities: it stores the note in a form that no older build sends to a model, and an older build may resume the transcript; and it sends no note to Remote Control's event lane.
@internal When false, the session recap (shown when you return after being away for 5+ minutes) is disabled. When absent or true, recap is enabled. Hidden from public SDK types until external launch.

@internal When the Client failed: `load` is before the module ran (its frame refused, the module not fetched, a throw at mount); `render` is a throw while drawing, an undrawable tree, or a render that never answered; `run` is a listener, timer or held closure, a loop, a flood. The hooks reached see it as `e.phase`.
@internal When true, Claude keeps working until the PR is ready for you to merge, a cron/Monitor is armed to resume later, or it hands you a self-contained next step.

@internal When true, a process whose newest system/init lists the capability `read_file_live_reply_v1` publishes the success reply only to the clients attached at that moment, as a control_response marked live_only: true on the session's unsequenced event stream, and the reply is not stored with the session's events. Send it only to such a session, and only if your client reads control_response frames from that stream; a reply sent while its stream is down is lost and the request must be sent again. A reply of over 56 KiB as JSON comes back instead as the live-only error `The reply is too large to be sent without storing it`, which is not stored either: ask for less with `max_bytes` and read on with `offset` (40,000 bytes as base64 fit beside up to 3,000 bytes of paths as JSON, `absPath` and any `requested_path` together). Every other error reply, and every reply from a process that does not list the capability, is an ordinary stored reply, so a client that sets it must accept either.

@internal When true, emit the totalTokensReminder block after each regular user prompt and (for 'padded-countdown') re-anchor the task budget to the full configured value at the start of each user turn. When false, the reminder appears only in the system prompt and after each tool-result batch, and 'padded-countdown' counts down over the whole session. Defaults to on. Env var CLAUDE_CODE_TOTAL_TOKENS_REMINDER_AFTER_USER_TURN overrides; server-controlled via GrowthBook tengu_lapis_anchor_user_turn.

@internal When true, the CLI never moves a call to this server's tools to a background task on its own: not after the auto-background delay, and not early for a priority 'now' message, which instead interrupts the turn and so ends the call. Meant for a server whose calls wait on a person. The turn waits for the call's own result, up to the server's timeout, so set timeout too. A tool that advertises MCP task support can still run as a task. Any value but true counts as unset. Read when the server is first registered, from initialize, mcp_set_servers or --mcp-config.

@internal When true, the caller means to hand the file on, for example into an artifact that other people can open, so a file that every other gate has passed also goes through Claude Code's test for credential files (takenByPathRefusal). One whose path has a credential's name or place, as sent or as it resolves, or is too dressed or too deep for the test to judge, is refused with the error_code credential_name (read_denied with the anchor as_written); one of Claude Code's own files, or a kernel or device path, is refused with no error_code. A file with more than one hard link is served: a caller that minds looks for itself. Only an answer that has `upload_screened` used the member. A CLI that predates it, the Remote Control bridge that a session itself runs, the engine's readFile and a session that reads through a tool container ignore it and answer as for a plain read_file, so a caller must take a success without `upload_screened` as a file whose name was not tested.

@internal When true, the request does not change the model. `model` must name a model: if it is absent, null, empty or 'default', the request fails with error_code 'invalid_request'. `system_prompt` is required: without it the request fails the same way. If `model` names the session's model, the request succeeds, and `system_prompt` replaces the custom system prompt as that member describes. The request makes no server check of the model, runs no PreModelSwitch hook, and sends no model report to the host. For a model id that this build knows, two names are one model if they resolve to one model id: an alias resolves to the id that it stands for, every dated id of a version resolves to the undated id, and a [1m] tag is ignored. An id that a behaves_as mapping points at another model is a different model. If the session's model is another model, the request fails with error_code 'model_not_current' and changes nothing. The request also fails that way while the session's records of its model disagree. A fallback that changes the session's model can cause that state until its turn ends, or longer. A session whose model setting is 'opusplan', 'opusplan[1m]' or 'haiku' runs a different model in plan mode. For such a session the request always fails with 'model_not_current'. A value that is not a boolean fails with 'invalid_request'. `claude -p` and a claude-code-server worker implement this member. Remote Control refuses every value but false. A build without this member ignores it and applies the request as a plain set_model.

@internal Where the auth token and the API key come from when both are configured (for example ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and '/login managed key'); the terminal then warns that auth may not work as expected. Source names only, never credential values. Absent when at most one is configured, when one apiKeyHelper supplies both, and from CLIs older than this field.

@internal Where the caret stands after the write instead of after the placed text: a UTF-16 offset into the whole draft the composer then holds, whatever `mode` placed the text. The app clamps it to the end of its draft, and moves one inside a character to the start of that character. Omitted when the fill names none.

@internal Where the element's handler lives: the plugin whose hook drew it and the handle its environment keeps the closure under, stamped by the engine as the tree left that hook. What a ui_press, ui_input or ui_select names the element by; a redraw that changed anything hands out new handles.

@internal Where the host got this server, for the data flow records of calls to it: one of Anthropic's, by its registry id; a claude.ai connector, by its id (tagged or a bare UUID) and its directory id or null; or one the user configured, by the transport the host reaches it over. The first two are taken only in a session a desktop host started. Without it, or with a value of another shape, the records say unknown (docs/desktop-host-contract.md, D139). Read from initialize, mcp_set_servers and the Agent SDK's server config, not --mcp-config, when the server is first registered.

@internal Where this hook may run when a cloud session is driven from this machine. 'device': offer it to the cloud session and run it here even when its script sits where the cloud session can write on this machine or cannot be pinned — the author accepts that the session may have changed files this hook executes. 'skip': never offer it to cloud sessions. Omit for the default: a command hook whose script could be read and pinned and lies outside everything the cloud session can write here is offered; other command hooks are not. Applies to this entry only: the same hook written in another settings scope keeps its own setting. An unrecognised value reads as 'skip' (the file still loads; the hook stays on this machine).

@internal Where this hook may run when a cloud session is driven from this machine. 'skip': never offer it to cloud sessions; 'device' or omitted: offered (an HTTP hook has no script to pin). Applies to this entry only. An unrecognised value reads as 'skip' (the file still loads).

@internal Whether Remote Control can be offered at all in this deployment (isRemoteControlDeploymentAvailable: not hard-disabled by managed settings, not nested in a remote environment, first-party provider). Only host-lifetime-stable conditions; transient ones (auth state, the GrowthBook rollout gate, the async org-compliance verdict) are deliberately excluded since hosts latch this from one initialize response — see the helper docstring. Lets IDE hosts hide their Remote Control affordance where it can never work. Absent (older CLI) → treat as available.

@internal Whether an IDE host that connects Claude in Chrome itself should connect it when the session starts. True when the "Enabled by default" setting (claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled) is on, this session did not connect the server itself, and the gates the terminal applies to the setting at startup pass (claudeInChromeDefaultForHost). Sent only to a host that owns the session's startup (isVscodeHostOwnedStartupSession). Absent (older CLI, other hosts) → treat as false.

@internal Whether any loaded plugin hooks `ui.render` for this component, and always true for `Theme`, which the engine answers itself; false means the surface may stop asking for it until the next ui_invalidate.

@internal Whether the CLI resolver says Remote Control should auto-enable at session start (explicit setting → policy default → GB rollout), so IDE hosts can mirror TUI behavior. Absent (older CLI) → treat as false.

@internal Whether the `managedSettings` in this initialize are the ones the process stored at launch under --managed-settings-in-initialize, so a re-sent initialize with the same settings also reads true. True does not say that they are in force: state.parentSettingsIncluded of list_permission_rules says whether they count beside the machine's own managed settings. The request's `managedSettings` field sets nothing after launch. Absent when the request carried none, on CLIs that predate this field (those never read `managedSettings`), and from responders that do not store them.
